claims.text: The as-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits sizeable caloric effects near 300 K under approximately 1 T magnetic field and 100 MPa pressure.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack.
The alloy's poor integrity and cracking arise from a coarse, inhomogeneous microstructure with localized residual stresses.
The proposed treatment consists of room-temperature HPT at 6 GPa for five full rotations.
HPT is followed by annealing at 400 °C for 30 minutes with controlled cooling.
HPT followed by low-temperature annealing will produce an ultrafine-grained, homogenized microstructure.
The proposed treatment will reduce microstructural flaw sizes.
The proposed treatment will make residual stresses more evenly distributed.
Severe plastic deformation will induce extensive grain refinement in this alloy.
A refined microstructure and more homogeneous stress field will impede crack initiation.
A refined microstructure and more homogeneous stress field will impede crack propagation.
The post-HPT anneal will relieve excessive dislocation density.
Relieving excessive dislocation density while retaining grain refinement will preserve the magnetostructural transition responsible for the caloric effect.
The proposed treatment will significantly improve ductility relative to the unchanged alloy.
The proposed treatment will significantly improve load-bearing integrity relative to the unchanged alloy.
The proposed treatment will preserve the alloy's large magnetocaloric response around 1 T and 300 K.
The proposed treatment will preserve the alloy's large barocaloric response around 100 MPa and 300 K.
The predicted benefits apply under static or cyclic mechanical loading typical of refrigeration applications.
